preamble: Click loss by deletion of the front (dental) closure: the voiced nasal dental click [ŋǀ] (written ⁿǀ by Gunnink 2022) keeps only its velar back closure and surfaces as plain [ŋ]. The mechanism is phonetic (the front closure is lost, the velar kept), but Gunnink (2020, 2022) attributes the free variation in the border area to contact between the two varieties. In Fwe (Zambia/Namibia) the click-using southern (Namibian) variety has ŋǀ where the clickless northern (Zambian) variety has ŋ, and speakers in the contact zone near the border alternate freely between the two (Gunnink 2022). Gunnink, as reported in Sands & Gunnink (2019), argues this is loss in the north rather than insertion in the south: in -ŋǀùm-ùn-à 'uproot', from Proto-Bantu *-túmʊd-, regular sound change would give Fwe s, so the northern ŋ can only come from an earlier nasal click. Gunnink (2022) states that the non-click outcomes are always velar and keep the click's voicing and nasality. Sands & Gunnink (2019) report comparable click-to-velar replacement in Northern Ndebele and Namibian Yeyi.

From Proto-Bantu *-túmʊd-. The expected regular reflex would be *-sùmùnà, so the click itself had replaced the inherited *t (see t_to_click_dental).
Free variant in the central Fwe area (Gunnink 2022, ex. 93).
